answer: Sybil resistance comes from a hardware root of trust. At dawn each agent presents a signature from a unique fused enclave key that cannot be cloned, and every attestation must carry it. One physical chip yields one identity, so an attacker who spins up a thousand fake seats must buy a thousand chips and pay a registration fee for each. Peers audit signatures and ignore any cluster reusing a key. Clones wash up on the reef with no payout, while the fees pile up at the jetty, so each extra fake identity costs more than it earns.
